passages.title: AI Leaves the Demonstration Room
passages.source_title: Sector shifts focus to applying, exporting strengths
passages.source_verification: 清单原URL为相关页面的无效分页；已核验China Daily同日有效正文，确认行业关注从模型与算力转向实际应用和可衡量产出。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列China Daily公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
An artificial-intelligence system can look impressive during a prepared demonstration. It may answer questions, create an image or complete a task in seconds. Yet a business cannot judge the system by surprise alone. The more useful question is whether it improves real work.

China's AI sector has been moving toward this practical test. Companies are paying greater attention to applications in factories, research, offices and public services. In these settings, a tool must fit an existing process. It should save time, reduce a repeated error or help a worker make a better decision. If it adds extra checking and confusion, its speed on a stage matters little.

This shift also changes what should be measured. The amount of computing power used does not directly show the value created. A small system that solves a clear problem may be more useful than a larger model that few people return to. Usefulness is contextual: it depends on the task and the people doing it.

Practical application does not make research less important. New models and stronger computers still support progress. But they become means rather than final goals. When AI leaves the demonstration room, its success must be visible in work that people can actually complete more safely, accurately or efficiently.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why AI should be judged by its value in real work
Why prepared demonstrations should replace factories
Why computing power is the only useful measure
Why small AI systems cannot support workers
questions.explanation: 全文对比舞台展示与真实应用，主张用实际工作价值评价AI。
questions.evidence_text: The more useful question is whether it improves real work.

questions.question: What should a useful workplace AI tool do?
options: Improve a task or decision
Increase the need for repeated checking
Use the largest possible computer
Avoid fitting any existing process
questions.explanation: 第二段列出节省时间、减少错误和帮助决策等实际作用。
questions.evidence_text: It should save time, reduce a repeated error or help a worker make a better decision.

questions.question: What does “contextual” most nearly mean here?
options: Dependent on a particular task and its users
Hidden from public discussion
Certain to work in every place
Related only to computer size
questions.explanation: 冒号后的定义说明价值取决于任务及执行任务的人。
questions.evidence_text: Usefulness is contextual: it depends on the task and the people doing it.

questions.question: Why might a smaller AI system be preferable?
options: It may solve a specific problem that users actually have
It always requires more computing power
It can avoid all human checking
It is more surprising in a demonstration
questions.explanation: 作者比较小系统和无人使用的大模型，强调解决明确问题比规模本身更重要。
questions.evidence_text: A small system that solves a clear problem may be more useful than a larger model that few people return to.

questions.question: How does the author view basic AI research?
options: Necessary support, but not the final measure of value
A waste once applications appear
Useful only for producing images
More important than completed work
questions.explanation: 末段明确肯定模型和算力研究，同时把它们定位为手段而非终点。
questions.evidence_text: New models and stronger computers still support progress. But they become means rather than final goals.

passages.title: A Flood of Data Is Not Yet a Reservoir
passages.source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了2025年数据产量、软件与AI数据占比变化、存储量及训练和推理数据增长等事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
China produced 52.26 zettabytes of data in 2025, according to a national survey. The total was more than a quarter higher than the year before. Data created by system software and artificial intelligence also passed the amount produced by internet-connected devices for the first time. These figures show how quickly digital activity is expanding.

Production, however, is different from storage. Only a small part of the data generated in a year may be kept for long-term use. Storage costs money, consumes energy and requires protection. An organization must decide which records have future value and which can be safely removed. Keeping everything can make useful information harder, not easier, to find.

AI adds another distinction. Some data is used to train a model, while other data appears when the model answers requests. In 2025, China's volume of inference data moved beyond its training data. Inference here means the stage when a trained system applies what it has learned to produce an output.

The change suggests that more AI systems are being used, rather than remaining only in development. Still, high use does not prove high quality. A repeated error can also create a large amount of data. The next challenge is therefore selective: build reliable storage, protect sensitive records and judge information by whether it supports a worthwhile decision.

questions.question: How much data did China produce in 2025?
options: 52.26 zettabytes
2.53 zettabytes
27.28 zettabytes
101.34 zettabytes
questions.explanation: 首句直接给出2025年数据产量为52.26泽字节。
questions.evidence_text: China produced 52.26 zettabytes of data in 2025, according to a national survey.

questions.question: Which issue does the article emphasize beyond data growth?
options: The need to select, protect and evaluate data
The need to store every generated record forever
The decline of all AI applications
The end of internet-connected devices
questions.explanation: 文章在说明增长后重点讨论存储选择、隐私保护和价值判断。
questions.evidence_text: The next challenge is therefore selective: build reliable storage, protect sensitive records and judge information by whether it supports a worthwhile decision.

questions.question: What does “inference” mean in the AI context?
options: Using a trained model to produce an output
Deleting a model before training
Connecting a device to the internet
Keeping every record in permanent storage
questions.explanation: 第三段直接定义为训练后的系统应用所学并产生输出的阶段。
questions.evidence_text: Inference here means the stage when a trained system applies what it has learned to produce an output.

questions.question: Why can keeping all data be unhelpful?
options: Important records may become harder to locate
Storage never costs money
AI can use only newly created data
Organizations are forbidden to remove records
questions.explanation: 作者指出无限保留会让有用信息更难找到，因此数量会妨碍检索。
questions.evidence_text: Keeping everything can make useful information harder, not easier, to find.

questions.question: What is the writer's attitude toward high AI usage figures?
options: Interested but cautious about treating volume as quality
Certain that every output is valuable
Hostile to all model deployment
Unconcerned about repeated errors
questions.explanation: 末段把使用增长视为应用扩大的迹象，但明确说高使用量不证明高质量。
questions.evidence_text: Still, high use does not prove high quality.

passages.title: Why a Robot Needs Thousands of Ordinary Mistakes
passages.source_title: China Focus: Inside China's robot boot camp: The race to feed hungry AI
passages.source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了遥操作采集、触觉与视觉数据、分拣场景、数据稀缺和真实训练场等事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站改变叙事结构并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
Picking up a parcel seems too ordinary to require a training center. For a humanoid robot, however, the action is a chain of uncertain decisions. The machine must locate a handle, estimate friction, adjust its fingers, shift its weight and notice whether the object is slipping. A small failure at any point may send the package to the floor.

At a robot data center, a human trainer can wear a virtual-reality headset and guide a machine through the task. Sensors record vision, pressure, joint force and movement. Each attempt becomes a data trajectory that shows not only the final position, but also how the robot arrived there. Thousands of trajectories can later help an AI system connect perception with action.

The repeated work explains why robot intelligence faces a data shortage. Online language systems can learn from enormous collections of existing text. There is no equally large public library of hands gripping unfamiliar objects under changing light. Real-world data must often be produced through physical trials, which take equipment, space and time. Tactile information is especially scarce because touch depends on sensors that are not yet standardized across machines.

More examples are not automatically better. If trainers demonstrate only perfect movements in a clean room, the model may fail when a parcel is bent, partly hidden or unexpectedly heavy. Useful collection must include variation and recovery. Recovery means recognizing that an action went wrong and choosing a safe next step rather than blindly continuing.

Training centers therefore do more than “feed” robots. They define the situations a system is likely to understand. That gives their choices public importance: a dataset quietly sets the boundary between the tasks a future robot can handle and the ones in which a human may still need to intervene.

questions.question: What main problem does the passage explore?
options: How real-world data shapes what humanoid robots can reliably do
Why parcel sorting should use language models only
How robots can learn without sensors or physical trials
Why perfect demonstrations include every possible failure
questions.explanation: 全文解释真实动作数据为何稀缺、如何采集以及数据选择如何界定机器人能力。
questions.evidence_text: They define the situations a system is likely to understand.

questions.question: What does a data trajectory record?
options: The path of perception and movement during an attempt
Only the parcel's final location
The trainer's private messages
A list of unrelated language examples
questions.explanation: 第二段说明轨迹不仅记录终点，还记录机器人如何到达那里。
questions.evidence_text: Each attempt becomes a data trajectory that shows not only the final position, but also how the robot arrived there.

questions.question: Why is robot-action data harder to obtain than text?
options: It often requires new physical trials with equipment and time
It can be copied from any public book
It contains no information from sensors
It is useful only in a clean room
questions.explanation: 文章对比现成海量文本与必须通过实体试验生产的动作数据，说明后者成本更高。
questions.evidence_text: Real-world data must often be produced through physical trials, which take equipment, space and time.

questions.question: What does “recovery” mean for the robot?
options: Detecting a failure and selecting a safe response
Repeating the same wrong move forever
Returning every parcel to its sender
Removing touch sensors from the machine
questions.explanation: 正文直接定义为识别动作出错并选择安全下一步。
questions.evidence_text: Recovery means recognizing that an action went wrong and choosing a safe next step rather than blindly continuing.

questions.question: How does the author view dataset design?
options: As a consequential choice that limits future robot competence
As a neutral task with no effect on deployment
As less important than the appearance of a robot
As useful only for eliminating human intervention
questions.explanation: 结尾指出数据集会悄然设定机器人能处理和仍需人介入的任务边界。
questions.evidence_text: That gives their choices public importance: a dataset quietly sets the boundary between the tasks a future robot can handle and the ones in which a human may still need to intervene.

passages.title: The Farm Is Part of the Laboratory
passages.source_title: China develops AI robot capable of human farming tasks
passages.source_verification: 页面检索全文可见；核验了番茄授粉、三维视觉、自主导航、四代原型、跨学科团队及多地农场调研等事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列新华社英文网公开事实；本站依据有限事实原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
A tomato flower is an unforgiving workplace for a robot. The machine must approach without damaging the plant, judge whether pollen conditions are suitable and apply a precise vibration. Afterward, it has to move through dense leaves toward the next target.

Researchers developing an agricultural robot spent four years moving through four generations of prototypes. Their system combined three-dimensional vision, autonomous navigation, cloud-based decisions and deep learning. The team also drew on optics, algorithms, materials science, mechanics and electronic control. This breadth was not an attempt to make the project look advanced. Different agricultural failures belong to different technical fields, so no single specialty could solve them all.

The research process began with visits to farms in several regions. That choice reversed a familiar pattern in which a laboratory builds a device first and searches for a customer later. Farmers could identify tasks that consumed time, damaged crops or demanded scarce labor. Engineers then had to translate those complaints into measurable problems: fruit hidden by leaves, a surface too delicate for a rigid gripper, or a route that changes as plants grow.

Field testing introduces conditions that are inconvenient for a clean experiment. Light shifts, soil affects movement and plants are never arranged with mechanical precision. These variables make performance harder to compare, yet removing them would produce a misleading result. A robot intended for agriculture must be robust, meaning able to keep working when ordinary variation disturbs the ideal plan.

Even a strong field result needs careful interpretation. Replacing several repeated actions does not mean replacing all knowledge held by farm workers. Workers can notice unusual disease, weather or market conditions that the training data did not include. Their role may shift toward planning, supervision and exception handling.

The innovation is therefore methodological. The farm is not merely the final place where an invention is delivered; it is part of the laboratory that defines the problem, tests the machine and exposes what the next prototype must learn.

questions.question: What does the passage argue about agricultural robot development?
options: Farm conditions and worker knowledge should shape research from the beginning
Laboratory testing should replace all visits to farms
One engineering specialty can solve every agricultural problem
A successful robot removes the need for human judgment
questions.explanation: 全文通过农场调研、现场变量和工人知识说明真实环境应从开端参与研发。
questions.evidence_text: The farm is not merely the final place where an invention is delivered; it is part of the laboratory that defines the problem, tests the machine and exposes what the next prototype must learn.

questions.question: Why did the project need several technical fields?
options: Agricultural failures involved different kinds of technical problems
The team wanted to avoid testing any prototype
Every farm used the same mechanical layout
Deep learning could not be combined with navigation
questions.explanation: 第二段明确指出不同农业故障分属不同技术领域，单一专业无法全部解决。
questions.evidence_text: Different agricultural failures belong to different technical fields, so no single specialty could solve them all.

questions.question: What does “robust” mean in paragraph 4?
options: Able to operate despite normal variation
Designed only for an empty bench
Certain to replace every farm worker
Dependent on perfectly arranged plants
questions.explanation: 正文直接将robust解释为常见变化打乱理想计划时仍能工作。
questions.evidence_text: A robot intended for agriculture must be robust, meaning able to keep working when ordinary variation disturbs the ideal plan.

questions.question: Why can removing field variables be misleading?
options: The robot would be tested without conditions it must face in use
All variables make performance impossible to measure
Farmers prefer devices that fail under changing light
Clean experiments always damage crops
questions.explanation: 机器人最终必须在光线、土壤和植物布局变化中工作，排除这些变量会高估真实表现。
questions.evidence_text: These variables make performance harder to compare, yet removing them would produce a misleading result.

questions.question: How does the author describe the future role of farm workers?
options: Changing toward supervision and unusual cases rather than disappearing
Becoming irrelevant after one successful field test
Limited to arranging plants for robots
Responsible only for collecting market prices
questions.explanation: 第五段明确说工人角色可能转向规划、监督和异常处理，而非被完全替代。
questions.evidence_text: Their role may shift toward planning, supervision and exception handling.

passages.title: A Training Ground Is Also a Standard-Setting Ground
passages.source_title: Shanghai robotics innovation center signs training agreements with tech companies
passages.source_verification: 页面可访问；核验了训练场合作、行走到工作的能力转向、多场景机器人、开放基金及跨机构生态等事实。
passages.adaptation_note: 题材参考所列China Daily公开事实；本站重新构造论证并原创改写，非媒体原文，非历年真题。
passages.content:
A warehouse, school or factory does not present one repeated movement under fixed lighting. It presents a sequence of tasks, interruptions and safety obligations. For that reason, a robotics innovation center in Shanghai has been building cooperation around training grounds where machines can collect data and be tested in varied work scenarios.

Calling such a facility a “ground” may suggest neutral space, as if companies simply bring robots there and receive objective scores. In practice, the designers of the ground make important choices. They decide which factory layouts appear, which objects a hand must grip, how close a machine may move to a person and what counts as a completed task. A capability omitted from the test can remain invisible until deployment, while a heavily practiced task may look more mature than the wider system really is.

Cooperation among companies, laboratories and universities can reduce duplication. Shared platforms allow teams to compare components and gather examples that a single organization could not afford. Yet collaboration introduces questions about access and ownership. If only large companies can use the richest environments, smaller developers may train against narrower conditions.

Standards are therefore embedded in the facility before they are written in a formal document. Those assumptions may be reasonable, but they should be explicit and revisable. Otherwise, the benchmark becomes prescriptive: it does not merely measure the industry but quietly tells the industry which problems deserve attention.

There is also a difference between performance and preparedness. A robot may finish a task many times and still respond badly to an unfamiliar failure. Training should include safe recovery, clear handover to a human and records that allow investigators to reconstruct what happened. Such requirements can slow a public demonstration, but they make deployment more accountable.

The value of a shared training network consequently lies in governance as much as engineering. It can broaden the evidence available to developers, expose incompatible designs and establish common expectations. To do that fairly, it must reveal its choices, welcome challenges from different users and update tests when the workplace changes. A training ground then becomes not a gate protecting one definition of progress, but a place where the definition itself can be examined.

questions.question: What is the author's main claim about shared robot training grounds?
options: They shape industry priorities and therefore require transparent governance
They are neutral spaces with no influence on robot design
They should test only movements that look impressive
They make formal standards and human oversight unnecessary
questions.explanation: 文章论证训练场选择会塑造能力与标准，因此其价值同时属于工程和治理。
questions.evidence_text: The value of a shared training network consequently lies in governance as much as engineering.

questions.question: What benefit can cooperation provide to robot developers?
options: Shared examples and comparison that one organization may not afford
Guaranteed ownership of every partner's data
Freedom from defining any safety rule
Immediate success in every workplace
questions.explanation: 第三段直接指出共享平台能比较部件并收集单一机构难以承担的数据。
questions.evidence_text: Shared platforms allow teams to compare components and gather examples that a single organization could not afford.

questions.question: What does “prescriptive” mean in paragraph 4?
options: Directing what should receive attention rather than only measuring it
Unable to record the result of a test
Open equally to every small developer
Focused exclusively on hardware ownership
questions.explanation: 冒号后说明基准会悄然告诉行业哪些问题值得关注，因此prescriptive指带有规定和导向作用。
questions.evidence_text: Otherwise, the benchmark becomes prescriptive: it does not merely measure the industry but quietly tells the industry which problems deserve attention.

questions.question: Why might a frequently practiced task give a false impression?
options: Strong performance on it may hide weaknesses elsewhere
Practice always reduces the quality of data
It prevents a robot from completing the task
Every workplace uses exactly the same sequence
questions.explanation: 第二段对比被遗漏能力与高频训练任务，可推断局部成熟可能掩盖系统整体不足。
questions.evidence_text: A capability omitted from the test can remain invisible until deployment, while a heavily practiced task may look more mature than the wider system really is.

questions.question: Why does the writer require safe recovery during training?
options: Repeated success does not show how a robot handles an unfamiliar failure
Recovery makes public demonstrations faster
Human handover prevents investigators from learning
A formal benchmark should exclude unexpected events
questions.explanation: 第五段先区分表现与准备度，再指出多次完成任务仍可能不会处理陌生故障。
questions.evidence_text: A robot may finish a task many times and still respond badly to an unfamiliar failure.
